In many cities around the world, electric scooter sharing services have appeared on the streets. Users can find a scooter through a smartphone app, ride it to their destination, and leave it there for the next person. The services have become especially popular among young people and commuters who need to travel short distances.

Supporters say that electric scooters offer several advantages. They are cheaper than taxis and faster than walking, and they do not produce exhaust gases. Some city officials hope that scooters can help reduce traffic congestion by replacing short car trips. In addition, scooters can make it easier for people to reach train stations and bus stops that are too far to walk to.

However, the services have also caused problems. Many riders leave scooters on sidewalks, where they block pedestrians and can be dangerous for elderly people and people with disabilities. There have also been many accidents, as some riders travel too fast or ride without helmets. As a result, several cities have introduced strict rules, such as limiting speeds, requiring scooters to be parked in special areas, and in some cases banning the services completely.

Hospitals in several countries have started using artificial intelligence to help doctors. AI systems can analyze medical images such as X-rays in a few seconds and point out areas that may show signs of disease. Some hospitals also use AI to predict which patients are likely to become seriously ill, so that staff can give them extra attention.

There are clear benefits to this technology. Many hospitals face a shortage of specialists, and AI can help doctors handle a large number of cases more quickly. In some studies, AI has detected certain diseases as accurately as experienced doctors. Early detection can lead to more effective treatment and save lives.

On the other hand, there are concerns about relying on AI. If the data used to train a system comes mainly from one group of patients, the system may make mistakes when examining others. It is also unclear who should be responsible if an AI system gives incorrect advice. Moreover, some patients feel uncomfortable with machines being involved in decisions about their health. For these reasons, most experts believe that AI should support doctors rather than replace them.

In recent years, some companies have opened convenience stores that operate without any staff at the cash register. Customers enter the store using a smartphone app, pick up the items they want, and simply walk out. Cameras and sensors record which products each customer takes, and payment is made automatically.

These stores offer advantages for both businesses and customers. Companies can reduce labor costs, which is especially important in countries where it is difficult to find workers. Customers no longer have to wait in line, and the stores can stay open twenty-four hours a day without the need for night staff.

However, unmanned stores have not spread as quickly as some expected. The technology needed to track customers' purchases is expensive to install, and errors sometimes occur, such as customers being charged for items they did not take. Some people are also worried about privacy, since the stores collect detailed information about customers' movements and shopping habits. In addition, elderly people and others who do not use smartphones may find it difficult to shop in these stores, which has led some companies to keep a staffed checkout as well.

In many countries, it has traditionally been mothers who take time off work to care for newborn children. However, some governments are now encouraging fathers to take parental leave as well. In some countries, a portion of the paid leave is reserved for fathers, so that families lose it if the father does not use it.

Supporters say that such policies have important benefits. When fathers take leave, mothers can return to work more easily, which helps reduce the gap in career opportunities and pay between men and women. Research also suggests that fathers who spend time caring for their babies early on tend to be more involved in raising their children later.

Despite these benefits, the number of fathers taking leave remains low in many countries. Many men worry that taking time off will harm their careers or that their colleagues will have to do extra work. Some companies, especially small ones, also find it difficult to manage without employees for long periods. Experts say that changing workplace culture is just as important as changing laws, and that managers should actively encourage male employees to take leave.

Some cities are trying to develop their "night-time economy" by encouraging restaurants, museums, and other businesses to stay open later in the evening. Cities such as London and Amsterdam have even appointed officials whose job is to support business and culture at night. In Japan, there have also been efforts to attract foreign tourists by offering more evening entertainment.

The main purpose of these efforts is economic. Tourists who have more options in the evening tend to spend more money, and businesses that stay open later can increase their sales. Supporters also say that lively streets at night can make cities feel safer, as more people are around, and that new jobs are created for workers who prefer evening shifts.

However, the night-time economy also has drawbacks. Residents living near busy areas often complain about noise and litter late at night. Public transportation may not run late enough for workers and customers to get home safely. There are also concerns about the health of employees who work regularly at night. For these reasons, experts say that cities need to balance the interests of businesses, visitors, and local residents.

Upcycling is the process of turning unwanted items or waste materials into new products of higher value. For example, old clothes can be made into bags, and wooden pallets can be used to build furniture. In recent years, upcycling has become popular among individuals, and some companies have started selling upcycled products.

Upcycling has several benefits. It reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills and the need to produce new materials, which saves energy and resources. Many people also enjoy the creativity involved in making something unique from items that would otherwise be thrown away. For businesses, upcycled products can attract environmentally conscious customers and help improve their corporate image.

However, upcycling cannot solve the problem of waste on its own. The amount of waste that is upcycled is very small compared with the total amount produced. Upcycled products are also often more expensive than ordinary products, because they are usually made by hand in small quantities. Some experts therefore argue that while upcycling is a positive trend, reducing consumption in the first place is a more effective way to protect the environment.

An increasing number of restaurants have started using robots. Some robots carry dishes from the kitchen to customers' tables, while others cook simple meals such as noodles or hamburgers. Customers can also order food using tablets placed on their tables, which reduces the need for staff to take orders.

Restaurant owners say that robots help them deal with a serious shortage of workers. Robots can work long hours without getting tired, and they allow human staff to focus on tasks such as greeting customers and dealing with special requests. Some customers also enjoy the novelty of being served by a robot, which can attract new visitors to the restaurant.

However, there are also concerns about the use of robots. They are expensive to buy and maintain, which makes them difficult for small restaurants to afford. Robots sometimes break down or cannot handle unexpected situations, such as crowded spaces or customers with special needs. In addition, some people worry that the spread of robots will reduce job opportunities, especially for young people and part-time workers who depend on restaurant jobs for income.

In several countries, teachers work extremely long hours. In addition to teaching classes, they prepare lessons, grade homework, supervise club activities, and communicate with parents. Surveys have shown that many teachers work more than fifty hours a week, and the number of people who want to become teachers has been falling.

To address this problem, some education authorities have introduced measures to reduce teachers' workload. Some schools have hired assistants to handle administrative tasks, while others have begun to hand over the management of after-school clubs to local sports organizations. Digital tools have also been introduced to make grading and communication with parents more efficient.

Supporters say these changes will allow teachers to focus on teaching and improve the quality of education. However, the measures have also faced challenges. Hiring assistants and outside coaches costs money, and many schools, especially in rural areas, have difficulty finding suitable people. Some parents have also expressed concern that their children will have fewer opportunities to participate in club activities. Experts say that long-term solutions will require more funding and a change in expectations about the role of teachers.

Smart home devices, which allow people to control lights, heating, and appliances using their smartphones or voice commands, have become increasingly popular. Some systems can learn their users' habits and adjust the temperature automatically, while security cameras allow homeowners to check on their houses while they are away.

These devices offer a number of benefits. They make daily life more convenient, especially for busy people and for elderly people or those with disabilities who may find some household tasks difficult. Smart heating and lighting systems can also reduce energy use by turning devices off when no one is home, which saves money and helps the environment.

However, smart homes also raise concerns. Because the devices are connected to the internet, they can be targets for hackers, who may be able to access cameras or personal information. Many devices also collect data about their users' daily routines, and people may not know how this information is used. In addition, if the internet connection fails or the company providing the service goes out of business, some devices may stop working properly.

In many cities, residents have started using empty land to create community gardens, where they grow vegetables, fruit, and flowers together. Some gardens are located on rooftops or in spaces between buildings, and many are managed by volunteers from the local neighborhood.

Community gardens offer several benefits. They provide fresh food, which is especially valuable in poorer neighborhoods where healthy food can be difficult to find. Working in a garden also gives people exercise and a chance to spend time outdoors. In addition, gardens can strengthen communities by bringing together people of different ages and backgrounds who might not otherwise meet.

However, community gardens also face difficulties. In many cities, land is valuable, and gardens may be removed when the owner decides to sell the land for development. Gardens also depend on volunteers, and they can become neglected if people lose interest or move away. Some experts suggest that city governments should provide long-term support, such as protecting land for gardens and offering advice on gardening, so that these projects can continue.

Subscription services, in which customers pay a regular fee to receive products or services, have become very common. Many people now subscribe not only to music and video streaming services but also to services that deliver meals, clothing, or even furniture. Companies in many industries have started offering subscriptions instead of selling products only once.

For businesses, subscriptions provide a stable and predictable income. They also allow companies to build long-term relationships with customers and collect information about their preferences. For customers, subscriptions can be convenient, as they do not need to make purchasing decisions every time, and they can often try many products for a fixed price.

However, subscriptions also have disadvantages for consumers. Many people sign up for several services and forget about them, continuing to pay for things they rarely use. Some companies make it difficult to cancel subscriptions, for example by requiring customers to call during limited hours. In response, some governments have introduced rules requiring companies to make cancellation as easy as signing up and to remind customers before automatic renewals.

Some public libraries have begun staying open late at night or even twenty-four hours a day. In cities where many students live in small apartments without quiet places to study, libraries with longer hours have become very popular, especially before exams.

Supporters say that extended hours make libraries more useful to the community. Students can study in a quiet environment with free internet access, and workers who are busy during the day can use library services in the evening. Some libraries have also reduced costs by using self-service machines for borrowing and returning books during the night, so that only a small number of staff are needed.

However, longer opening hours have also caused problems. Some libraries have had difficulty ensuring safety at night, and a few have had to hire security guards, which increases costs. There have also been concerns about people using libraries simply as a place to sleep. Moreover, staying open longer means higher costs for electricity and heating. As a result, some libraries have decided to extend their hours only during exam periods rather than throughout the year.

Scientists have developed a way to produce meat by growing animal cells in laboratories, without raising and killing animals. Several companies are now working to make this "lab-grown" or "cultivated" meat available in supermarkets and restaurants, and a few countries have approved its sale.

Supporters believe that lab-grown meat could have major benefits. Raising livestock uses large amounts of land and water and produces a significant share of greenhouse gases. Producing meat in factories could reduce these environmental impacts. It could also improve animal welfare, since fewer animals would need to be raised in crowded conditions.

However, lab-grown meat faces several challenges. At present, it is much more expensive to produce than ordinary meat, and it is difficult to produce in large quantities. Some consumers are also unwilling to eat meat made in a laboratory because they believe it is unnatural or are worried about its safety. In addition, farmers' groups in some countries have opposed lab-grown meat, fearing that it could threaten their livelihoods. It remains unclear whether it will become a common part of people's diets.

In many countries, the number of households in which both partners work full-time has increased greatly. However, surveys show that in many of these households, women still do most of the housework and childcare. As a result, many working women feel that they have two jobs: one at work and another at home.

This imbalance can have serious effects. Women who carry most of the responsibility at home may have less time to develop their careers, and some decide to work part-time or leave their jobs. The stress of balancing work and family can also affect their health. Some experts believe that the unequal division of housework is one reason for low birth rates in some countries.

To address this issue, some companies have introduced flexible working hours and encouraged male employees to leave work earlier. There is also a growing market for services that reduce the burden of housework, such as meal delivery and cleaning services. However, experts argue that changing traditional ideas about the roles of men and women is essential, and that education from an early age can play an important role.

topic: Moving government offices out of the capital
passage:
In some countries, governments have considered moving certain government offices out of the capital city to regional areas. South Korea, for example, moved many government ministries to a new administrative city, and other countries have relocated agencies to smaller cities.

Supporters argue that such moves can bring several benefits. They can reduce overcrowding and high living costs in the capital, and they can help revitalize regional economies by creating jobs and attracting businesses. Spreading government functions across the country may also reduce the risk that a single disaster in the capital will stop the government from operating.

However, relocating government offices is not easy. Moving offices and employees costs a great deal of money, and many workers do not want to leave the capital, where their families and children's schools are located. Communication between government officials, politicians, and businesses may also become more difficult if they are located in different cities. Critics also point out that relocation alone may not be enough to revive regional economies unless other policies, such as improving transportation, are also introduced.

Every year, billions of disposable coffee cups are thrown away around the world. Although many cups appear to be made of paper, they are often coated with plastic, which makes them difficult to recycle. To reduce this waste, some cafés and cities have introduced programs that encourage customers to use reusable cups.

In some programs, customers pay a small deposit for a reusable cup, which they can return to any participating café to get their money back. Other cafés offer discounts to customers who bring their own cups. In a few cities, disposable cups have been taxed or banned altogether. Supporters say these measures can greatly reduce waste and raise awareness of environmental issues.

However, these programs have faced difficulties. Many customers forget to bring their own cups or find it inconvenient to carry them. Deposit programs only work well when many cafés participate, so that customers can easily return cups. Some cafés have also raised concerns about hygiene and the extra work involved in washing cups. Experts say that a combination of incentives and regulations is likely to be the most effective approach.

Short videos lasting only a few minutes have become an increasingly popular way to learn. On social media platforms, many teachers and experts now post short videos explaining topics such as history, science, and language. Some schools have also started using short videos in their lessons.

Supporters say that short videos make learning more accessible and enjoyable. Viewers can learn something new in their free time, such as while commuting, and the visual format can make difficult ideas easier to understand. For people who struggle to concentrate for long periods, short videos can be a good way to start learning about a topic.

However, some educators are concerned about relying too much on short videos. They argue that complex subjects cannot be fully explained in a few minutes and that viewers may gain only a shallow understanding. There are also concerns about accuracy, as anyone can post videos and some contain incorrect information. Furthermore, some researchers worry that watching many short videos may reduce people's ability to focus on longer texts and lectures.

As populations age, the number of elderly drivers has increased in many countries. In some places, a series of accidents involving elderly drivers has led to public debate about whether older people should continue to drive. Some governments have introduced tests that elderly drivers must pass when renewing their licenses.

Those who support stricter rules point out that physical and mental abilities, such as eyesight and reaction time, often decline with age. They believe that regular tests can help identify drivers who are no longer safe and prevent serious accidents. Some local governments also encourage elderly people to give up their licenses voluntarily by offering discounts on buses and taxis.

However, many elderly people depend on their cars, especially in rural areas where public transportation is limited. Giving up driving can make it difficult for them to go shopping or visit hospitals, and it may lead to isolation. For this reason, some experts argue that improving public transportation and developing safety technologies for cars, such as automatic braking systems, are just as important as introducing stricter rules.

Many companies are changing the way they train their employees. Instead of holding long training sessions that last a whole day, some companies now use "microlearning," in which employees study short lessons of five to ten minutes on their computers or smartphones.

This approach has several advantages. Employees can study whenever they have a few free minutes, so training does not interrupt their work as much. Short lessons may also be easier to remember, especially when they are repeated regularly. For companies, microlearning can be cheaper than traditional training, since there is no need to rent rooms or pay trainers to teach large groups.

However, microlearning is not suitable for every kind of training. Complex skills, such as leadership or negotiation, may require longer sessions with practice and discussion. Some employees also find it difficult to stay motivated when studying alone, and they may skip lessons if they are busy. For these reasons, many companies combine microlearning with traditional training, using short lessons to review and reinforce what employees have learned in longer sessions.

In Japan, the number of empty houses, known as akiya, has been increasing for many years. Millions of houses are now unoccupied, especially in rural areas where the population is aging and young people have moved to cities. Many of these houses have been left by owners who inherited them but do not live nearby.

Empty houses can cause a variety of problems. Buildings that are not maintained may collapse during earthquakes or storms, and they can become a fire risk. Abandoned houses can also make neighborhoods look less attractive and reduce the value of nearby properties.

To address this issue, some local governments have created "akiya banks," websites that list empty houses for sale or rent at low prices. Some offer financial support to people who move to the area and renovate old houses. These efforts have attracted families and young people who want to live in the countryside. However, many empty houses are in poor condition and require expensive repairs, and some owners are unwilling to sell or rent them. Experts say that more effective policies are needed to prevent houses from becoming empty in the first place.

Several companies are testing the use of drones to deliver packages. In some areas, drones are already delivering medicine to remote villages and small items to customers who live far from stores. Supporters believe that drone delivery could become common in the near future.

Drones offer several advantages over traditional delivery methods. They can reach places that are difficult to access by road, such as islands and mountain villages, and they can deliver urgent items such as medical supplies very quickly. Because they are powered by electricity, drones may also produce fewer emissions than delivery trucks. In addition, they could help solve the shortage of delivery drivers that many countries face.

However, there are still many obstacles. Drones can carry only light packages and may not be able to fly in strong wind or heavy rain. There are also concerns about safety, as drones could fall and injure people, and about privacy, since drones with cameras fly over people's homes. Noise is another issue, especially in residential areas. As a result, governments are carefully considering what rules are needed before allowing drone delivery to expand.

In recent years, more people have been trying to eat less meat. Some have become vegetarians or vegans, while others simply choose to have several meat-free days each week. Restaurants and supermarkets are offering more plant-based options to meet this growing demand.

There are several reasons for this trend. Many people are concerned about the environmental impact of meat production, which uses large amounts of land and water and produces greenhouse gases. Health is another reason, as some studies suggest that eating large amounts of red and processed meat may increase the risk of certain diseases. Animal welfare is also an important factor for some consumers.

However, reducing meat consumption is not easy for everyone. Meat is an important part of many traditional cuisines, and some people find plant-based foods less satisfying. Plant-based alternatives can also be more expensive than ordinary meat. In addition, people who stop eating meat need to make sure they get enough protein and other nutrients, such as iron and vitamin B12. Experts suggest that small changes, such as eating less meat rather than none at all, may be more realistic for many people.

Since the COVID-19 pandemic, many universities have continued to offer hybrid classes, in which some students attend in person while others join online at the same time. Universities have invested in cameras, microphones, and software to make this possible.

Hybrid classes offer greater flexibility for students. Those who live far from campus, have jobs, or need to care for family members can attend classes without traveling. Students who are sick can also join online instead of missing classes. Some universities believe that hybrid classes can help them attract students from other regions and countries.

However, many teachers say that hybrid classes are difficult to manage. It can be hard to pay attention to students in the classroom and those online at the same time, and online students often participate less in discussions. Technical problems, such as poor sound quality, can also interrupt lessons. Some research suggests that students who attend online tend to feel less connected to their classmates. For these reasons, some universities have decided to return to mainly in-person classes while offering online options only in special circumstances.

topic: Paying people to move to rural areas
passage:
Many rural areas are facing serious population decline as young people move to cities for education and work. To reverse this trend, some governments and towns now offer financial incentives to people who move to rural areas. These can include cash payments, free land, or support for starting a business.

Supporters say these programs can help revitalize communities. New residents can fill jobs, start businesses, and help keep schools and hospitals open. With the spread of remote work, more people are now able to work for city companies while living in the countryside, which makes such programs more attractive than before.

However, critics question whether these programs are effective in the long term. Some people move to receive the money but leave after a few years when the support ends. Newcomers may also find it difficult to fit into small communities with different customs, and rural areas often lack services such as public transportation and shopping facilities. Experts suggest that, in addition to financial support, towns need to improve living conditions and help newcomers build relationships with local residents.
